description: This line plot, labeled (b) “The performance on Llama2,” illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of knowledge probing after editing for five different methods—Base, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000), with tick marks at powers of ten. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 60% to 80% and is linearly scaled. Each method is represented by a distinct colored line with a unique marker: Base (black circles), FT (blue triangles), MEMIT (purple diamonds), IKE (red triangles), and ROME (green squares). Across the entire range of co-occurrence numbers, all lines show an upward trend, indicating improved accuracy with increasing co-occurrence. The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 73% and rising to about 78%. The Base method, which represents the unedited model, shows the lowest performance, beginning at roughly 61% and increasing slightly to about 65%. The other methods—FT, MEMIT, and IKE—fall between these two extremes, with their respective accuracies increasing from around 62–65% to approximately 70–75%.
